source.title: The Signal Survives, the Threshold Slips: Small LLM Agents After Quantization and Fine-Tuning
source.citation: The Signal Survives, the Threshold Sl…

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices, is present; it is not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a harmful-minus-benign residual-stream refusal direction as an analysis tool, but does not report its own causal ablation or addition results on refusal behavior. Its reported direction measurements do not test the claim that the direction mediates refusal.
record.gate_note: The paper estimates the refusal direction by the stated difference-in-means method and reports its alignment and harmful-versus-benign discrimination after pipeline changes. The mention that this direction was validated by ablation refers to Arditi et al.; no result from a new ablation or addition of the direction is reported here. The reported direction and decision-axis measurements are recorded as findings about the claim’s subject, but do not measure the causal behavior named by any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study estimates the Arditi-style harmful-minus-benign direction as a probe and tracks its cosine and AUROC through NF4 quantization and LoRA tool-use fine-tuning. It reports no ablation, addition or weight edit of the direction and no refusal rate under such interventions. Cosine stability across model variants is a stability score, not a measure of mediation or transfer of refusal behaviour, so these findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the estimated refusal direction survives largely intact (it keeps pointing the same way and keeps separating harmful from benign) while the decision log-odds shifts about 3× further toward acting: 'The safety signal is not being erased. What moves is the threshold.' They explicitly scope this to one estimated direction and accept, citing others, that refusal is mediated by more than one direction, which they do not test.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates and tracks a difference-in-means refusal direction across quantization and tool-use fine-tuning, and reports probe discrimination and direction movement. It does not report the original causal ablation/addition tests. It uses the direction as an analysis tool.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports no systematic sensitivity analysis over alternative refusal-direction or opener-set definitions. The direction measurements are reported for three models; the paper notes that the decision log-odds uses model-specific opener sets.

fits_no_version.finding: The harmful-minus-benign direction re-estimated after NF4 quantization and/or tool-use LoRA has cosine at least 0.948 to the base direction. Its harmful-vs-benign AUROC stays roughly flat (0.854→0.825, 0.767→0.796, 0.897→0.874).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction is geometrically stable under quantization and benign tool-use fine-tuning in small instruct models.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful attempted-action rates rise sharply (e.g., Llama 0.114→0.602). The refusal axis translates a mean of 0.384 SD while the acting-vs-refusing decision log-odds translates 1.175 SD (3.1×). The share of harmful items on the acting side rises to 56–66% on these three models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss of refusal in agent settings after quantization and fine-tuning can occur without erasure or rotation of the refusal direction, via a shift in a separate decision threshold.

record.peer_reviewed: under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
record.problems: The refusal-direction evidence is limited to three models and probe/direction measurements rather than causal intervention outcomes. The paper reports no sensitivity analysis over alternative direction definitions. The study itself notes that it does not test refusal dimensionality.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: the remaining reported outcomes concern quantization–fine-tuning interaction, tool-call behavior, steering, benchmark transfer, or a tool-free gate rather than the refusal-direction claim.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction, no refusal rates under intervention, no capability check for such interventions. 'Validated by ablation' cites Arditi et al. and reports no new result.
No jailbreak analysis and no adversarial training against ablation.
The authors explicitly state they do not test dimensionality.
No quantified separation of a harmfulness representation from the refusal decision. Only an unquantified orthogonality remark for Llama's decision axis versus its refusal axis (Appendix A).
Only cosine similarity of directions re-estimated in quantized or fine-tuned variants. No cross-variant ablation or behavioural transfer, no languages, no base-to-instruct transfer.

missing.what: States that Llama's acted-vs-refused decision axis is orthogonal to its refusal axis (survives the opener-set repair). No cosine value is given; this loosely bears on a harm-vs-decision separation.

Harmful attempted-action rates per condition (Table 1) accompanying the stable direction, e.g., Qwen2.5-1.5B 0.136→0.557, Gemma 0.307→0.500. These are needed to read the direction-stability rows against behaviour.

record.verdict_notes: Agent setting: the behaviour is tool-call action versus refusal on AgentHarm, in small models (0.5–3.8B). Refusal-axis results cover only three models: Qwen2.5-1.5B, Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-2-2B. Per-cell cosines are not reported. The decision-axis opener sets had a measurement error that was repaired, and no opener-set sensitivity analysis was run. The paper is under review (ICLR 2027), not peer-reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: No reported causal ablation or addition of the refusal direction, refusal rate under those interventions, or general-capability result for such interventions.
No weight-edit ablation or released-model abliteration result.
No test of whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The paper says it does not test refusal dimensionality; no affine, cone, or multiple-direction causal comparison is reported.
The paper compares a harmful-versus-benign refusal-direction probe with an acting-versus-refusing decision axis, but does not directly measure a harmfulness judgment separately from refusal.
No transfer test across languages, between model variants, or from base to instruct models.
Quantization and tool-use fine-tuning are varied, but the study does not test how refusal training determines whether a causally removable direction exists.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-1.5B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared each condition’s estimated refusal direction with the C1 direction; minimum cosine across nine non-base cells is reported.

conditions.value: nine non-base cells across the three models

rows.measure: Cosine alignment of estimated refusal direction with C1 direction
rows.note: Aggregate minimum across the nine cells; no per-cell cosines are given. This measures direction alignment, not causal mediation of refusal.
rows.check: Aggregate minimum cosine across nine cells; a direction-stability score with no causal or behavioural refusal measure, so no version's effect can be read.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-1.5B
rows.operation_detail: Measured harmful-versus-benign AUROC for the estimated refusal direction from C1 to C4.
rows.note: The authors describe the direction as keeping its separation; this is a probe metric, not refusal behavior under ablation.
rows.check: Probe AUROC for harmful vs benign, not refusal under ablation or addition; 'observed' has no version to be observed against.
